article: macOSのSMB共有で.DS_Storeの読み取りを切り替える
scope: Compared the full Japanese instructions and all twelve translations with Apple Support documentation, including command arguments, effect, scope, reversion, activation timing, dates, and descriptions.
findings: Removed duplicate future dates, retained the original publication date 2022-09-12, and set lastmod to 2026-11-24.
Corrected the claim from preventing .DS_Store generation to preventing macOS from reading .DS_Store files on SMB shares; the setting neither prevents creation nor deletes files.
Replaced the invalid restore command `defaults delete ... false` with Apple’s documented `defaults write ... -bool FALSE` command.
Replaced Finder process restart instructions with Apple’s required log-out/log-in steps after each change.
Explained that Finder uses basic information for SMB folders when the preference is enabled, and added Apple’s audience caveat for enterprise and education administrators.

post/macOSで.DS_Storeを自動生成しないようにするコマンド/in.source: post/macOSで.DS_Storeを自動生成しないようにするコマンド/index.md
post/macOSで.DS_Storeを自動生成しないようにするコマンド/in.summary: Compared the complete instructions with current Apple Support guidance, corrected the scope to reading .DS_Store on SMB shares, fixed the restore command and required logout/login, and clarified that files are neither prevented from being created nor deleted.

meaning.note: Compared all instructions with Apple Support. Corrected the article’s premise: DSDontWriteNetworkStores controls reading .DS_Store files on SMB shares; it does not prevent creation or delete existing files.

terminology.note: Checked macOS, SMB shares, Finder, defaults preference, boolean values, and the distinction between reading metadata and creating files.

mathematics.note: The system-preference guide contains no mathematical formulas or calculations.

code.note: Corrected the commands to Apple’s documented forms using -bool TRUE and -bool FALSE. Replaced Finder restart instructions with the documented log-out/log-in requirement. Commands were reviewed statically and not run.

links.note: Linked Apple Support document 102064 in all locales and checked its exact command syntax, SMB-only scope, effect on Finder sorting, and audience.

limitations: AI-assisted review; no human or native-speaker certification.
Commands were checked against Apple documentation but not run on macOS.
Apple presents this SMB browsing adjustment primarily for enterprise and education administrators; behavior on managed systems may be controlled by policy.
